“When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”, Esau, seeing “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, went his own rebellious way anyway. “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling, and that is where the light-skinned Arabs come from.

Jacob went toward Haran, and at a certain place he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, “and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” The Lord promised, “the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. That is all four corners: before they were even born, it was prophesied that Jacob’s seed would be found in the four corners of the earth, scattered among the families of the earth, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” And the Lord promised, “I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven”, a portal to paradise. He set up his stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” He vowed the tenth, the tithe.

Keep Bethel in mind. On the map it sits right under Shechem, the place where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan and where Rehoboam was later crowned. These early holy places all lay in the land that would become Ephraim’s.

The division between Ephraim and Judah did not begin at the split of the kingdom; it was building long before. Part of it goes back to Joseph, the father of Ephraim.

Joseph was raised up to tell Pharaoh what was coming: “Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land”, and “it shall be very grievous”. “And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.” Joseph prophesied the famine and showed Egypt how to prepare for it, and by it Israel was saved when Jacob and his sons ran down to Egypt.

The same pattern ran through Abraham. After the Lord told him, “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house”, he came from Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates, up to Haran, and down into Canaan, the stretch called the Fertile Crescent. When famine struck Canaan, Abraham ran to Egypt too, just as Jacob and his house later did. The parallels line up.

So Joseph’s house carried a great deal: Joseph saved Israel in the famine, and later Joshua, of Ephraim, divided the land. That is part of why Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and why the rivalry that tore the kingdom in two was already there long before Rehoboam.

“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.
blog/2026/2026-01-31-2026-01-31-my-templ: God gave a law of the beasts to make a difference between the clean and the unclean. So “every creature” being good means good for its purpose, not good to eat; pork stays unclean no matter who prays over it.
Meats are received by those who believe and know the truth, and “thy law is the truth”. So what makes the meat clean is the word of the law, not a prayer said over a plate of pork.
“He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment.” Truly believing means keeping the law about clean and unclean meats, not departing from the faith by eating whatever you like.

Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.
blog/2026/2026-02-01-2026-02-01-the-divi: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar.” Loving God and loving your brother go hand in hand, so whoever hates his own people is still in darkness: God and race.
The new commandment John writes is the one Christ gave: “love one another”. That love is how all men know his disciples, and the one who loves his brother abides in the light.

“Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart” was already in the law, so Christ's new commandment is the old one Israel had from the beginning but was not following. Bear no grudge against your own people; love them.
The old commandment from the beginning is the greatest: “Hear, O Israel”, love the Lord with all your heart, and “love thy neighbour as thyself”. Love your people, love your ways.

At Bethel the Lord promised Jacob, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. Israel would be everywhere on the earth, through captivity and through migration, forced or willing. And the promise goes on, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: that is the Israelite families in those lands, north, south, east and west. The nations are not the ones blessed; their blessing is servitude.

Then the Lord renamed him: “Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”. “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”. In context that can mean all twelve tribes, but prophetically it is written that way for the division to come: the nation is the southern kingdom, Judah, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom, Ephraim. The kings out of his loins are Saul, David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

Moses shows where the division came from. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” He kept us “as the apple of his eye.” “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”, rich, comfortable and rebellious, and “lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”, which is Christ. So the Lord said, “I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Isaiah names who is not a people: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people”, after the northern kingdom joined Syria against Judah.

Hosea says the same of the company of nations: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Ephraim became as Gentiles, heathens, the uncircumcision. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Yet the number of Israel “shall be as the sand of the sea”, as promised to Jacob, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”, and that head is Christ. Ezekiel agrees: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The hatred between the nation and the company of nations is why both fell, the north first and Judah after. The law always said, “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, and “he that hateth his brother is in darkness”. Esau never forgets and holds his grudges, while Jacob in captivity forgets his own and cares more for his oppressor. The people that enslaved us tortured us, beat us, raped us, castrated us and hid our history for hundreds of years, and now they are ruling: that is their heaven, and we are in hell. Imagine being in the heathen's hell and teaching the devil in his kingdom the access he has to heaven, our heaven. That's hate. You hate your people and you hate yourself, and for that you are in darkness. In captivity, your people being oppressed, and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. Love your people and love your ways, and the nation and the company of nations become one again.
blog/2026/2026-02-07-2026-02-07-a-soul-w: Christ “hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God”, his blood upon the altar. So we walk in love and become that same sacrifice for our brothers and sisters.

The blood makes atonement for the soul, and through Christ “we have now received the atonement”, reconciled while we were enemies. His blood is more powerful than animal sacrifice, the ground we build on by grace.

When Rachel wanted a child and came demanding one from Jacob, “Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Jacob could not give what only God gives. Go ask God for that baby.

That is the same answer for the single sister who points at leadership because she has been here five, six, seven years and has no lord, while a sister who came after her already has one. Leadership is not in God’s stead. If you want a lord, go ask God, and ask him what he wants you to change first. Check yourself: maybe talk to the sister who came after you and ask how she did it, instead of calling it hatred from leadership. God put leadership in your life to watch over your soul. Be the Proverbs 31 woman, fix your mouth, do the work on the body, stop eating the ice cream at night, and know your size before you point at the fit brother. It is not something you deserve; it is something you earn, by sacrifice.

The same dumb spirit Christ cast out of the boy tells that sister to go into the world, get a lord, and bring him in, when in the world she caught nothing before. Go into the world and you are still the same negro, still the same woman; you never changed, because you would not go to the Lord. Some came here for the ride and not the work. One sister reached out to a man in the world, and he is gone; another left for a man online who said he did not believe in two or three wives, then found out he did. Some of you are not going to get a lord in this captivity, and if that is what you came for, Satan will move you out of the way.

That spirit is the one that “ofttimes” cast the child “into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”: the paycheck spent in the club that gets sprayed up, the drunk drive that costs your limbs, the mob on Eastern Parkway, in the mix of a bunch of no-good negroes up to no good. Leaving your house to go with the dumb negroes is a dumb spirit. We thought it was cool; it was a dumb and deaf spirit, not listening and not seeing our condition. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth”: your belief is your power. When Satan keeps attacking you, your faith is weak, so cry like the father, “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”

“This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Some demons are higher than others, so fast and pray, and do not let it conquer you. And once made whole, hear Christ: “sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The world you left two years ago is not the world you would go back to; sin has multiplied, and worse demons are jumping on people.
blog/2026/2026-02-08-2026-02-08-edom-s-a:
“In this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil”. There are children of God on the planet, and there are children of the devil on the planet. And “whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of God, neither he that loveth not his brother. For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another”.

“Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Wait: we thought Cain was of Adam. It says no. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of that wicked one, of Satan. That is exactly what God told Cain in Genesis 4: unto thee shall be his desire, and he shall rule over thee. “And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.”

This is the enmity of Genesis 3:15 made plain: “between thy seed and her seed”. Satan’s seed is Cain, the children of the devil, and her seed is Israel, the children of God.

Cain’s line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob. Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Idumea, the Greek and Roman name for Edom, is that same Esau. So when we ask who the children of the devil are in the earth today and why they hate us, John has already told us: not as Cain, who was of that wicked one.

Paul speaks of the man of sin: “Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”. His coming is after the working of Satan, meaning Satan is his father, as he was Cain’s. That is Esau, Cain come again.

Genesis 3:15 ends, “it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.” Christ is our head, smitten so that the sheep were scattered. But the heel is Edom’s Achilles heel. Jacob took hold of Esau’s heel at birth, and in Daniel 2 “a stone was cut out without hands, which smote the image upon his feet that were of iron and clay, and brake them to pieces.”

The image is the empires. The head of gold is Nebuchadnezzar and Babylon; the silver is Persia and Media; the brass is Greece, “which shall bear rule over all the earth.” That was Alexander, “son of Philip, the Macedonian”, who “slew the kings of the earth” until “the earth was quiet before him; whereupon he was exalted and his heart was lifted up”: the beginning of white supremacy in the earth. His kingdom was parted among his generals, “and evils were multiplied in the earth.” Their own books, The Chronology of Ancient Nations and The Rise of Christendom, trace Philip back to Esau. The iron is Rome, and we are still in it: America and NATO, a kingdom “partly strong, and partly broken”, strong in military, with the toes as the European nations. The miry clay is the melting pot: “they shall mingle themselves with the seed of men: but they shall not cleave one to another”.

The stone is Christ, “Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone”. He strikes the image on its feet, its heel, and “the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth.” And “in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people”. We are living in the days of these kings. What we teach is the beginning of that kingdom, and it cannot be stopped; it will consume all these kingdoms with the word of God.

In the garden, before Adam and Eve were put out, God said, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Enmity is hatred. Satan has seed on this earth, and the woman’s seed, the descendants who would come through her, is Israel. When that was spoken, Cain was not yet born. The seed of Satan was Cain.

Genesis 4 shows how. “And the Lord said unto Cain, Why art thou wroth? and why is thy countenance fallen? If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted?” If you obey me, will you not be accepted by me? But “and if thou doest not well”, if you choose to break my commandments, “sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The one spoken of there is Satan: Satan would be Cain’s desire, and would rule over him. Satan would be Cain’s god and Cain’s father.

Cain chose not to obey, and he killed Abel. From that moment the enmity of Genesis 3:15 was at work in the earth: the seed of the serpent against the seed of the woman.

It did not end with Cain. His line died in the flood, but all spirits return. Cain came back as Esau, the one who “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, and Abel, or Seth, came back as Jacob, whose hand took hold on Esau’s heel. So Genesis 3:15 and Genesis 4:7 explain the hatred Edom has for Israel to this day: it is the enmity God put between the two seeds in the beginning.

“And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth”. Don’t you see something wrong there? Abel was already dead, and Cain was still alive. So why does it never say that Cain was in Adam’s image?

Go back to the making of Adam: “And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle”. Adam, the black man, was made in the image of God. Adam and Eve had Cain and Abel; Cain killed Abel, because God had told him that if he did not do well, sin lay at the door and Satan would rule over him.

Then, when it names the son born “in his own likeness, after his image”, it names Seth, not Cain. People say everybody is in the image of God. No: Cain was not in the image of God, and he is never said to be in Adam’s image.

So whose image was Cain in? John answers it: Cain “was of that wicked one”. Seth was of Adam; Cain was of Satan. That is why the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent are two different seeds, and why Seth’s line, the line that returns as Jacob, is the one that carries Adam’s image.
blog/2026/2026-02-14-2026-02-14-fighting:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.
blog/2026/2026-02-14-2026-02-14-prepare-:
“Wherefore, my dearly beloved, flee from idolatry”. That is in the New Testament, for you black Christians, you black apologists, you black pastors who say the law is done away with. Why would Paul write it if the law was done away? Because it goes right back to Exodus 20: “Thou shalt have no other gods before me”.

“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”. That is where 1 Corinthians 10:14 comes from.

Valentine's Day is idolatry; its origin is Februus and Lupercalia, a fertility rite in which women presented themselves to be struck because it was believed to help with fertility. When you sit up there and celebrate Valentine's Day, you are putting Februus, whoever the hell that is, and Lupercalia before the Lord. What's wrong with Christmas? It's idolatry. Your birthday? Idolatry. Halloween? Idolatry. That's what's wrong with it.

The Lord gave us our own high holy days, in Leviticus 23. The Destruction of Nicanor began last night at sundown, the victory recorded in 1 Maccabees 7 and 2 Maccabees 14 and 15, when Judas Maccabeus defeated and killed Nicanor, the Seleucid Syrian Greek commander who came to crush Israel and threaten the temple. Tonight at sundown begins Purim, when we were saved from being wiped out in the Persian Empire: the enemy was Haman, and the deliverance came through Esther and Mordecai. Our enemies' holidays, the Fourth of July and Christmas, are victories over us. Ours are victories over our enemies. Flee from their idolatry and keep what the Lord gave us.
blog/2026/2026-02-14-2026-02-14-the-iran:
Ezra foretold that “the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars of the wood, and with great power shall they come, and join battle with them, and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Carmanians are the Iranians: Carmania was a region of southeastern Iran, the modern province of Kerman, part of the Persian Empire, and Persia only formally became Iran in 1935. Why the Assyrians? In antiquity Assyria conquered Israel, took the northern kingdom, and moved into our land. That is exactly what Esau-Edom has done with our land today. They are not the rightful inhabitants; they are thieves, and the Lord is against them.

Ezekiel says so: “Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it”. Who is Mount Seir? “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” So the prophecy is against Esau-Edom, and the Lord says, “I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.”

Why? “Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it”. The two nations are the northern kingdom, Ephraim, and the southern kingdom, Judah: they took those two nations by identity theft, robbing us of who we are. The two countries are the United States of America and Israel. The children of Israel were in both first, and the whole world was made for our sake, but Edom stole both lands.

They said, “and we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there”. They possess it as if the Lord were with them, by calling themselves Jews and Christians. So “I will even do according to thine anger, and according to thine envy which thou hast used out of thy hatred against them; and I will make myself known among them, when I have judged thee.” The same way they hate the Israelites, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans, the Lord will use that same anger against them, and they will know that God did it.

Christ names them too: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” He knows our poverty, “but thou art rich”, because the promises and the covenant belong to us.
The Lord fed and clothed Israel, yet “she did not know that I gave her corn, and wine, and oil”, and she gave it to Baal. That is how they forsook the Lord God of their fathers and served Baalim.

The law forbade letting children “pass through the fire to Molech”, yet Israel grew bullheaded and followed the gods round about them anyway. That stubbornness is our history, and why we are in captivity.
blog/2026/2026-02-21-2026-02-21-the-vant:
To covet is not simply to desire. It is to want what belongs to another inordinately: you violate God's laws to get it. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”. The daughter belongs under the father just like everything else in his house. Go around him to get her, never telling the fathers or the elders, and you have coveted. To entice is to allure, to bait, to induce to evil; it is trickery and deception. “My son, if sinners entice thee, consent thou not”. And “Love worketh no ill to his neighbour”: if you love the sister, how did you use ill means to get her?

Peter shows what we are supposed to be doing instead: “Whereby are given unto us exceeding great and precious promises: that by these ye might be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust. And beside this, giving all diligence”.

As brothers and sisters come in here, you are supposed to be escaping these worldly elements and truly repenting. When you look across the aisle, you are supposed to be looking for righteousness, not just her behind. Taking your sister for lust is the corruption that is in the world, and the same thing goes on on the other side. A man who talks to you under cover, without your father and without the leadership, does not have good intentions; the fact that he didn't do it the right way shows you where his mind is.

Do it with diligence, the right way. When we announce our marriages we say, this is the day the Lord has made between you two; you can bring forth righteousness right here, and the Lord, the angels and everybody are in agreement with it. When you do things the right way, you have a whole community behind you. The fathers and the elders have the vantage point: we see down the road where it is going, and we make the decision as fathers.

Exodus 22:17: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins”. He has to pay, but he still is not getting the daughter. Somebody might say, he paid, so he gets to take her. Leviticus 6 shows the principle: “Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away”.

Took violently away. To entice that daughter against her father's wishes is to violate him, and violation is violence. That is the same reason a man who steals an ox must “restore five oxen for an ox”: the owner was violated, and restitution is paid for the violent act against him.

“or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten”. The recent matter was deceit. Her fathers didn't know anything about it, the leadership didn't know anything about it, nobody knew until her sister discovered it, and they still weren't going to say anything. How are you going to come up later saying, here's the law?

“Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering”. The principal is the actual thing taken, and the fifth part is added on top. So you are not getting the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why the judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, to be beguiled by a wicked brother who says we're applying Exodus 22:16. That's a damn lie.

The Pharisees came to Christ “tempting him, and saying unto him, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every cause?” They were trying to use Moses' law, the writing of divorcement in Deuteronomy 24. Christ took them back to the beginning: “Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh?” From the beginning there was no such thing as divorce. What are you talking about, quoting Moses? It's the same as a negro trying to quote Exodus 22:16.

“Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder”. God did not put these backdoor marriages together. That's why love worketh no ill to his neighbour: you will not do evil and call yourself love. You don't love anything but your own lust.

“Why did Moses then command to give a writing of divorcement, and to put her away? He saith unto them, Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so”. The only reason Moses had to bring in that negro-proof law is that we were hard-headed and gave Moses hell. It is a failsafe law, a kind of bylaw to keep us from going all the way wicked. You are not supposed to be in failure at all for it even to come up, and quoting one after you went off and did wrong does not make you righteous.

That is covering violence with the garment: “for one covereth violence with his garment, saith the Lord of hosts: therefore take heed to your spirit, that ye deal not treacherously”. The Pharisees enlarged the borders of their garments, and the fringes represent the laws. A man who deceived to get a sister and then gives her a so-called law from the Bible is covering his violation with the law. Sisters and brothers, watch yourselves, hold yourselves in the diligence of the scriptures, and stop playing games.

Christ says, “except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.” We claim we want the days shortened, but we are not ready, because wicked brothers are trying to slide in. Brothers and sisters who come from the world with a world mentality would love nothing more than to seduce and defile you, men and women both, because they don't want to change. Negroes don't like change. They pretend they've changed and put on the fringes and the border of blue so you let your guard down, then work behind the scenes to allure you away from your protection.

Dinah shows how it happens, and she was not raped. “And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.” Was she snatched? No, she went out on her own. With a father and twelve mighty brothers, you know they brought her the wisdom that pertains to a woman, and tried to keep her in straitly, the way the scripture says to keep a shameless daughter. She did not want to hear it. She wandered away from her father and her brethren.

“And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.” Something in her spirit let him know. He knew whose daughter she was, and he saw she was not rolling in the spirit of her fathers or her brethren. That is how slick brothers hit sisters in the DMs: they read your spirit when you are not studying, and once they talk that talk, you feed right into it.

“And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.” That is the part that tells you it was not rape: he spake kindly to her. You gave him your ear, he got your underwear. She was enticed, beguiled, allured: drawn away from her protection, from her fathers, from how she was raised, from the protections leadership put around her. Enticing is covetousness; she belonged to Jacob, and he drew her away. Then he asked to marry her, and her brothers said no, you already defiled her. She had to live with that stain for wandering out of her father’s care, and you read nothing of her after that.

Christ warns, “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect”: some of you men and women of the third slated to make it. Everybody with fringes and a border of blue is not right; do not look at his pretty beard. One who tells women marriage is not the goal and singleness is not the curse, while flaunting his own wife, is the devil in black flesh; he wants the women to stay in sin. A woman in the world turned down one of these street preachers when he broke character to ask for her number. A woman in the world knows more about the commandments than a negro with fringes and a Bible who is supposed to be keeping them, yet a sister in here will entertain the same kind in her DMs. Whoremongering brothers fake the funk, become soldiers, and look for spinsters, sisters anxious about getting older and not married yet, and gas them up, because all bread is sweet to a whoremonger. That is why, when you correctly come together, you exchange medical records and show each other; leadership does not need to see them. Give diligence and study, so you can recognize deception at your door, whatever it is wearing.
blog/2026/2026-02-28-2026-02-28-power-un:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.
blog/2026/2026-02-28-2026-02-28-the-vant: When no one keeps this law, the Lord has a controversy with the land, “because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land”. Whoredom breaks out into lying, killing and adultery: the land full of wickedness.
blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-marriage:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.
blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-wars-are:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.
blog/2026/2026-03-08-2026-03-08-hope-ami:
The foundations of the kingdom of heaven are the same stones, the same gems, that the high priest wore. “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work”: cunning work means make it look fancy. It has to be dope; it has to look good, not corny. It is made “of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.”

“Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.” It was designed like a square, the same height as it was wide, just like the kingdom, where the length and the breadth and the height are equal.

“And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones”: sardius, topaz and carbuncle; emerald, sapphire and diamond; ligure, agate and amethyst; beryl, onyx and jasper. And “they shall be set in gold in their inclosings”, the gold holding them in.

“And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” These stones are the names of the children of Israel. Revelation 21 says the same thing about the kingdom of heaven: its foundations and its gates carry the twelve tribes. The Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20 is built on Israel.

Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people”, and Isaiah 25 shows why: those fierce nations will be subdued. “Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.” The terrible nations, the ones that made everyone afraid, will themselves fear the Most High.

“For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.” That is us. Verse 4 is Israel: the poor and the needy that the terrible ones have been blasting against like a storm, and God has been our refuge through it.

“Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers”, and that goes right back to verse 3: the city of the terrible nations shall fear. Then, “the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low”: their branch, their people, brought low. So when Isaiah 33 says we shall not see that fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, it is because God has brought them down.

Psalms 122:5 says “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles where those thrones are: “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

The thrones in Jerusalem are thrones for judging the twelve tribes. That is why Psalms 122 says it is whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, and not all nations.

So the quiet habitation of Isaiah 33:20, the city of our solemnities, is the seat of the kingdom, with Christ's table and the thrones of the house of David set in it.

“I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let's go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit. “Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width. Revelation 21 shows it: the city lieth foursquare, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, measured by the angel, its foundations garnished with the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28, the stones with the names of the twelve tribes.

“Whither the tribes go up.” Wait a minute. Where all nations go up? No: whither the tribes go up, “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony of Israel, because that kingdom is what was always prophesied. The kingdom is not for everybody.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Luke 22:30 shows those thrones, sitting on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and Revelation 20:4 shows who sits on them: the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus, who had not worshipped the beast, the white man's kingdom, nor his image, his religion and his politics, nor received his mark, his lies in their foreheads, their minds. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

Psalms 140 proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” Psalms 68 said scatter the nations that delight in war; don't you see Trump and them delighting in war?

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You thought it would end with Venezuela. Oh, no. He said we are going to hit Iran. You thought it ended there; next week Mexico, and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say. Don't you hear them mocking the nations? They wanted to land in Spain, Spain said no, and now they are mad and talking about Spain. And “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: this so-called white man, keep me from their hands. Then, “preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” They purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.” Traps all around.

These are the fierce nations of Isaiah 33:19. When the Lord scatters them, we shall not see that fierce people any more, and Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation.

Isaiah 33:20 says to look upon Zion and see Jerusalem “a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down”. Habitation meaning at rest, at peace. Like a tent with stakes driven down, not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up, and not one cord broken.

Psalms 46 says the same: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.”

“The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved”: all the heathen nations, the same ones we read about in Isaiah 33:19, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we cannot understand. Their kingdoms shall be moved. And “he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.” God is our refuge; it is true.

So the nations are moved, but Jerusalem is not. She shall not be moved, because God is in the midst of her.

“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” The mountain of his holiness is Jerusalem.

“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” This is the Zion that Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon: “Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities.” It is the city of the great King, the joy of the whole earth.

So the quiet habitation Isaiah saw is not a small thing. It is the city where the Lord is greatly praised, beautiful for situation, and it will never be taken down again.

“The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.” Why bring them again? Because God's people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.” Damn! Our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies, and those nations that run their mouths against us, the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” That is the sanctuary. “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.” People singing before the Lord, not like these churches: beautiful songs, with men and women behind them playing instruments and young girls with timbrels. “Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” Little Benjamin because they almost got wiped out, and they are the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. This is his re-established kingdom.

“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute. “Rebuke the company of spearmen”, the soldiers, “the multitude of the bulls”, the people that have power in the other nations, “with the calves of the people”, their little ones, “till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute. Then, “scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is? The white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War. They delight in war.

This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20: the temple standing, the tribes gathered, the kings bringing tribute, and the fierce nations subdued.

“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. Then, “let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: let the heathen nations be judged in his sight. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must learn that they themselves are only men. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

Then read Isaiah 33:19 again: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” Why? Because they shall be subdued. It is “a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand”: that is the other nations, whose languages we do not know.

The nations have acted like gods over Israel. The Most High puts them in fear so they know they are but men, and then they are subdued and forced to worship the King. That is why we will not see that fierce people again.

“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments made manifest are his prophecies and his laws coming to pass before everyone's eyes.

This is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” When all nations come and worship before the Most High, they are no longer fierce against Israel. They are subdued. That is what the Lord is saying here: these nations will be brought down and made to come and worship before him.

So the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, the nations whose languages we cannot understand, will not be seen raging against us any more. They will be bowing before the King, because the Lord only is holy and all the nations will fear him.

“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122.

Then “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that is great tribulation. They are the ones “which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man, this kingdom. Nor “his image”: his religion, his politics. And they had not “received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not receive his lies in their foreheads, in their minds.

And so “they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those who come through great tribulation without bowing to the beast are the ones who sit on the thrones in the Jerusalem Isaiah 33:20 describes, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

Psalms 122 says “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, and Revelation 21 shows what that means: “the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”, measured “with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” It is as tall as it is wide.

Twelve thousand furlongs is about 1,500 miles by man's measurement, but it is not man's measurement: “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” It is angelic measurement, so the size is not what we are thinking.

And “the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” Garnished means decorated: all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst. Each stone represented one of the tribes, the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls”, “and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.”

And the city “had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” So the kingdom is not for everybody. This is the Zion Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon, the tabernacle that shall never be taken down.

Zechariah shows what it looks like when the nations are subdued: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Those that are left are the ones who came against Jerusalem. These nations are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. Year after year they must go up and keep the feast of tabernacles, the very feast they never kept.

That is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” The fierce nations with a stammering tongue will not be fierce any more; what is left of them will be worshipping the King, the Lord of hosts, at Jerusalem.

blog/2026/2026-03-21-2026-03-21-much-is-: Israel is a holy people because the Lord is holy and has “severed you from other people, that ye should be mine”. He chose them to be a special people unto himself, above all people.

Christ was moved with compassion on the multitudes scattered “as sheep having no shepherd”. That love is what moves leaders to deny themselves the riches and the women, keep his commandments, and rebuild the nation.

People are watching. A sister came to the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and not one brother tried to talk to her. That is the right example: a people made in God's image, living by the breath he gave, set apart from every other nation.
