“Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” God says he will deal himself with the seed of the oppressor mixed in; so don't worry about it, brothers, just teach. “Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb.”

Joseph was blessed with “blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.” When Ephraim mixed with the murderer, that same blessing was turned: a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. The root of the fruitful bough is dried up because of the mixing.

“They shall not dwell in the Lord’s land; but Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things in Assyria.”

Ephraim shall return to Egypt: that is the spiritual Egypt of Revelation 11:8, “the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt.” The Joseph who once ruled Egypt has returned to Egypt again, this time in captivity, in the western hemisphere.

And there they eat unclean things. Just like Ephraim, so all the tribes, as Ezekiel 4:13 shows. The same captivity and the same defiled bread fall on the whole house of Israel among the nations.

Jacob called his sons together in Egypt to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and highlight those last words: the last days. Of Joseph he said, “Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall.” By a well: they would live by the waters, on islands, in the last days. The walls are forts like El Morro, built by the Spanish to keep the other European powers out of places like Puerto Rico. “The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him”: the conquistadors sorely grieved him. “But his bow abode in strength.”

The Spaniards' own records, gathered in the book Lost Tribes and Promised Land, bear this out. Duran found Judaic customs in the old Aztec religion, unleavened bread on certain days and bathing for purification, and came to believe the Indians descended from the lost tribes of Israel. In 1644 an Indian guide named Francisco declared that his countrymen would be avenged upon the Spaniards in time by means of a people now hidden. Montesinos, a Judaizer imprisoned by the Inquisition, was reciting the formula of the New World Marranos, Blessed be the name of the Lord, who has not made me an idolater, a barbarian, a negro, an Indian, when he stopped and told himself, Those Indians, they are Hebrews. Indians later came to Antonio de Montesinos and recited the Shema in Hebrew, Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one, and told him they were of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. That is Puerto Rico, with Manasseh in Cuba.

That people now hidden is Judah, and the Psalm uses the same words the record used: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Israel is God's hidden people, and the nations have taken crafty counsel against them. The Spaniards' records, which they collected and kept, testify of the hidden ones the Bible speaks of.

Sirach speaks to those in the middle of the trial: “Ye that fear the Lord, wait for his mercy; and go not aside, lest ye fall.” Don't go aside; don't say, I want to leave this truth and do something else. If you do, you will fall.

“Ye that fear the Lord, believe him; and your reward shall not fail.” “Ye that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for everlasting joy and mercy.”

“Look at the generations of old, and see; did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, and was forsaken?” Was Job confounded? No. Was Joseph forsaken? No; what his brethren meant for evil, God meant for good. “For the Lord is full of compassion and mercy, longsuffering, and very pitiful, and forgiveth sins, and saveth in time of affliction.”

That is the close of Joseph's story: wait on the Lord, go not aside, and he saves in the time of affliction.

Endure to the end, and God shall restore everything. Job is the proof: “And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.”

His brethren and sisters and old acquaintances came and ate bread with him, “and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him.” “So the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: for he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she asses.” He had seven sons and three daughters, Jemima, Kezia and Keren-happuch, “And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job.”

Joseph's life ran the same way: sold, slandered, imprisoned, and then made ruler over Egypt, with his brethren falling down before his face. The latter end was greater than the beginning. Whatever you are suffering, endure it; God turns the captivity of those who hold on, and blesses their latter end more than their beginning.

When Jacob died, Joseph's brethren were afraid: “Joseph will peradventure hate us, and will certainly requite us all the evil which we did unto him.” They sent a messenger begging forgiveness, “And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.” Then he said, “Fear not: for am I in the place of God?” “But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.”

Only a spiritual man can understand that. Joseph was on another level of understanding. He sat back and reflected on everything that happened to him, the pit, the slavery, the lie, the dungeon, and knew it was God's divine plan. He may not have understood it while he was in the midst of it, but going through the seven years of plenty and the seven years of famine he realized his purpose. God set that whole thing up.

Paul gives the precept: “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” We all go through things we don't understand while we are going through them, asking why God is doing this to me and nobody else. There is a purpose.

All things means all things: poverty, health problems, eviction, trials, tribulations, temptations, whatever it is. If you love God, you must endure it to the end, as Joseph did, and it will work together for good.

For Ephraim's envy and Judah's vexing to end, both kingdoms must keep this law: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, nor “bear any grudge against the children of thy people.” That is the way to salvation.

“Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”, and that neighbour is the children of thy people, your own nation. Ephraim and Judah must learn this, because no one enters New Jerusalem with hatred in their heart.

Paul still kept the day of atonement, since “the fast was now already past”, but he did not sacrifice, because his faith was in Christ. The fast itself is not the problem.
These men fasted and sacrificed, yet turned “the grace of our God into lasciviousness”. Their devotion had no honour against the flesh, and those same spirits are back today.

When Christ said “He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death”, he was quoting the law. Here is where he was getting it from: “And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.”

You curse your father and mother, you shall surely be put to death. But I’m mad at my father and mother, I’m going to curse him? Okay. Well, you are going to have a short life.

That is what Colossians 2:8 means by beware of the tradition of men: the tradition of the elders set the child free from his parents, but the commandment of God says the one that curses them shall surely die.

“Beware lest any man spoil you through philosophy and vain deceit, after the tradition of men”. To see what the tradition of men does, go to the scribes and Pharisees.

“Then came to Jesus scribes and Pharisees, which were of Jerusalem, saying, Why do thy disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? for they wash not their hands when they eat bread.” The tradition of the elders means oral traditions passed down. They had a tradition that you had to wash your hands from the tip of the finger up to the elbow before you would eat.

Here is his answer: “Why do ye also transgress the commandment of God by your tradition? For God commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.” That is the fifth commandment, honour thy father and mother, that thy days may be long upon the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

“But ye say, Whosoever shall say to his father or his mother, It is a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free.” The tradition was that a child could declare himself a gift and be free from obeying his parents. It is what they call emancipation today: America has the same thing, get to sixteen and get away from your parents.

“Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition.” The Pharisees were following traditions that contradicted God’s laws. That is the tradition of men Paul warns about in Colossians 2:8: whatever sets aside the commandment and is not after Christ.

“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

That is Simon. He hated Onias, his brother, and his faction committed murders. This is the domino effect: it starts off as coveting; Simon coveted power. From there it turned to anger, from there to slander, and from there to murder. It is never just one sin, and not only are you affected, the people you sinned against are affected too.

Holding on to anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. You are drinking poison waiting for somebody else to drop dead, and they are not dropping dead. The only one being affected is you. This goes for men and women.

“There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.”

Simon did all three. The slander of a city: God does not like that thing, and Simon slandered the city. The gathering together of an unruly multitude: Simon had all the Greeks gather together to try to get the money from Jerusalem. And a false accusation: he accused Onias of doing this to Heliodorus. God said all these are worse than death.

Then think about this: don’t tell me what they say about me, tell me why they feel so comfortable telling you. In every school there is that one brother or sister that all the murmurers draw to, and they tell them all the things they don’t like about people. Why do they draw to you? You obviously did not have our back, because they are slandering and they feel so comfortable saying evil to you.

A deacon once pointed out a sister in red shoes with high heels and called her a hoe because of the shoes. The Bishop called Deacon Asaf, Deacon Malachi and the others over and asked them if she was; they said no. And he blew that brother’s spot up in front of them. You cannot come to me with evil. We must train ourselves to hate evil.

“Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.”

Use not to make any manner of lie, not a big one and not a small one. The custom of it is not good: when lying becomes your custom, it becomes what you are.

This follows the false witness of Exodus 20:16 and the maul, sword and sharp arrow of Proverbs 25:18. Simon made a custom of lying: he betrayed the money, slandered Onias, and called a man zealous of the law a traitor. These are basic laws, and our people must keep them.

Simon “was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.” He was so bold he called Onias the high priest a traitor, that type of a brother, a man zealous of the law.

These are basic laws, but for some reason in the black community they are so difficult. Just so, so difficult. Simon broke this one outright when he falsely accused Onias before the Greeks, and everything that followed came out of that false witness.

“But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. Simon hated Onias the third so much that he had one of his men kill one of Onias’s priests. That is why it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins. James shows where it comes from.

“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain”. Simon wanted the upper hand over Onias, and he could not get it. So what did he do?

“ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” Because you are not praying to the Lord about it. “Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you pray and still do not receive, it is because you ask for the wrong reasons. You have a lustful purpose behind it, a purpose that is not for the benefit of the nation.

This is a self-examination class for all of us: these are the attributes of Simon.

“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.”

Every neighbour will walk with slanders. “And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity.”

There are people who love the slander. They teach their tongue to speak lies, and they are very good at it; there are some very good liars out there. You ever see a woman caught in the midst of adultery? She starts crying: this is not what it looks like. And some men will dismiss what they saw with their own eyes. Some of you are such a simp.

Don’t bring anybody like that around. They cannot roll with us. Let them stay over there with those other camps. That is what Simon was: a brother that supplanted, walked with slanders, and would not speak the truth about Onias.

“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.”

What does that mean? Whatever the judgment is on that man, you get the judgment. This is why in the hood, in the ghetto, people see murders all the time and say, I’m not saying nothing. Then weeks later, a month, a year, that same person ends up dead, and you say, what did she do, they never killed nobody. No: they were a witness, and they chose not to utter it.

Read on and the law also says “if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.” And when he is guilty, “he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing”.

A story from camp: the brothers were planning who to take traveling, and one brother’s hair was unkempt. He was told to trim it, and he answered, well, I guess I’m not traveling then. A couple of men heard it. A young man from Detroit told what was said, and when the officer who heard it first was questioned the next week, he said, I heard it, I was going to tell you next week. Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.

Be mindful of brothers. They may seem decent on the outside, but you have to be mindful of the things they say, or don’t say.

“Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”.

It does not start with the murder. It starts with anger at your brother without a cause. “and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”. Raca means thou fool, vain fellow, and the council there is man’s council.

“but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.” Just continuing the sin, the name calling and all of that, puts you in danger of hell fire. That is when God has to step in.

These are the attributes of Simon, and the class is a self-examination for all of us. Simon’s anger toward Onias turned into slander and name calling, calling him a traitor, and it ended in murder.

“A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.”

Why is he a maul, a sword and a sharp arrow? Because that man will get people hurt, and will get people killed. A false witness is a weapon.

That is what Simon’s false witness against Onias became. He called the high priest a traitor, and before long “by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. His lie was a sword in the hands of his faction, and it drew blood among his own people.

“This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias”. Simon of the tribe of Benjamin revealed the secret of the money to the Greeks and then slandered Onias the third, telling them Onias was the one who did that to Heliodorus. This Simon was no damn good.

Now look at the ones who stand next to that kind of man: “Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.”

The type of man who is a partner with it hates his own soul. He hears the cursing and does not tell it. He keeps it tucked in. That goes directly against the law in Leviticus 5, where the one who hears and does not utter it bears the iniquity.

So it is not only the Simon who is guilty. The one who stands by, hears the evil, and keeps quiet is partnered with him, and he is hating his own soul.

“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.”

There is a lot of slander in the Israelite community; Deacon Asaf has been going over it in classes these last two weeks. There are camps that thrive off slander, hatred, name calling, ridicule and false accusations.

God already told you he is going to cut off people who do that. Cut off means he is going to kill them. So for you to join with these people, you are nothing but a fool.

And the high look and the proud heart come from the slander; that is what they do. They think God is with them, and the men and women around them, as stupid as they are, believe God is with them. God is not with them, not according to these scriptures.

Simon slandered Onias the third. So how serious is slander? “For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.”

Slander is not a light thing. It is the first step of a counsel against a man’s life. The ones who slander take counsel together, and what they devise is to take away his life.

That is exactly the road Simon walked. He slandered Onias to the Greeks, and it did not stop at words: “when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. The slander of many leads to the taking of life.
blog/2026/2026-06-27-2026-06-27-the-negr:
Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

God promised to “remember the covenant of their ancestors”, and the New Testament says the same: he came to show “the mercy promised to our fathers, and to remember his holy covenant”. Bloodline matters, because the covenant runs through the fathers.
blog/2026/2026-07-04-2026-07-04-job-sees:
Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

That was the attribute Job had: “the cause which I knew not I searched out.” The Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and they searched the scriptures daily to see whether the things they were taught were so. That made them more noble.

We have to be the same way. Search things out daily. Do not just hear it and move on, and do not come asking without having looked first. A father to the poor, a judge in the gate, and a man who searched out what he did not know: that is the kind of man Job was, and the kind we have to become.

“Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” Job is telling you what he used to do. The fatherless are the orphans, and he delivered them and the ones who had no one to help.

That goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.”

Job judged the way God judges. And he did not stop there: “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words and do not know what to say to bring them comfort. Job knew exactly what to say. Then he comforted the widow, mourning and crying because her husband just died.

That is a hard thing. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words. You have to let a dying believer know, it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right. When we die, that is not the end of it for us, and that is what comforts us.

“When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!” What does that mean, he prepared his seat in the street?

“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.”

So Job was a judge. He sat in the gate and judged the people with just judgment. That is why “The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.” When Job rolled on the scene, everybody shut the hell up. Princes covered their mouths, young men moved the hell out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted him. The nobles held their peace; they had nothing to say either. That is total respect and honor.

“As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”. What is the secret of God? This shows the relationship between Job and us.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. The things revealed belong to us and to our children for ever, and they are revealed for a purpose: that we may do all the words of this law. The secret of God was upon Job’s tabernacle because he was of that people, and he kept that law.

“And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.” They waited for his words with their mouths open. When he was teaching or giving counsel, he was dropping blessings on them, dropping understanding.

It says the same thing as the song of Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”.

So when Job spoke, it was like that: “my speech dropped upon them.” And that right there is prophetic. It is going to come again in the future, near to come.

“My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.” Job was up there. He was no pushover, no punk.

This is what Jethro told Moses: “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God”.

That is what Job was doing. He was for the people to God-ward, bringing their causes to God, and men waited in silence for his counsel. “After my words they spake not again”: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. “I chose out their way, and sat chief”: he counseled them and directed them, and dwelt as a king in the army.

“I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job did not know, he searched out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff. Don’t fake it. Job said, if I did not know it, I searched it out.

Christ said it: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.”

We have to get to that point. Search it out. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, get your Zondervan Bible dictionary, get the complete works of Josephus, get your concordance, and do your own work. Before you ask us a question, how about you search it out, and then ask your question after you have done research on it. That is what Job did with every cause he did not know.

Job looks back on his life: “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”. When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. But what does “by his light I walked through darkness” mean?

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is the lamp, and the law is the light.

That is the light Job walked by. We can only walk through darkness the way Job did: with God’s commandments. Job kept the law, and that law was the light that carried him through a dark world.

“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

“Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

That is why it was written down beside Job 29:14. Sometimes you just scribble in your Bible, and when you look at it again you see why. God wants his priests clothed with righteousness, and Job put on righteousness and it clothed him. His outward robe and diadem matched the righteousness he walked in, and the saints shout for joy when the righteous are clothed that way.
blog/2026/2026-07-04-2026-07-04-woe-to-a:
The angels pulled Lot into the house and smote the men at the door with blindness, and even blinded they wearied themselves trying to find the door. Then the angels took Lot out and gave them one order as the cities burned: don't look back. “And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.” “But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.”

Why would she look back? The city was being destroyed; she had just seen what happened in front of her house. She should have been glad to escape. Somebody was not vexed with the filthy conversation of that city; there was something in it she missed. That is why Luke also says, if you put your hand on the plow and look back, you are not worthy.

Christ said it in three words: “Remember Lot’s wife.” That is a warning for all of us: don't look back. You are in this truth now. Stop worrying about the long-lost cousin and auntie, stop trying to be friends with everybody and please people, stop dropping by the house on their birthday. Focus on this truth and stay away from filthiness, or be destroyed just as Lot's wife was destroyed.

Judgment is coming to Esau, as Sodom's came. “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” We have to come out of her mentally, come back to the law, statutes and commandments, stop playing around in the truth, and keep the faith of Christ, without looking back.
blog/2026/2026-07-18-2026-07-18-as-in-th:
Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Jacob's blessing lays it out. “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the sceptre is the kingship. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: between the feet means the loins, the seed. The lawgiver comes out of Judah's loins, which shows there is no immaculate conception. “until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes.

That is why Paul tells them “be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled.” In his time many were running around saying the resurrection had come and gone already. Paul reminds them not to let anyone deceive them; Christ had not returned, and the gathering belongs to him alone, when he comes.

The falling away means the twelve tribes of Israel have to fall and go into captivity, and Luke 21:24 shows it.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “and shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem taken over by other nations, in particular the Edomite nations, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until that time of rulership is over.

So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all twelve tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed, the son of perdition. Perdition means eternal damnation, spiritual ruin and hell; it comes from the Latin perdere, to destroy or to lose. It is the fate of the wicked, the absolute loss of one's soul, the final loss of salvation and unending punishment.

The Lord shall consume that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth”, and 2 Esdras 13 shows the Son doing it: “this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest.”

Those wicked inventions are the ICBM missiles and all that technology, their satellites spread across the globe. Christ will rebuke all of it and “shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame.”

Then: “he shall destroy them without labour by the law.” He will not need their weapons; the law does the destroying. God is saying his law is fire, the same fire that is in the mouth of those who teach it. That is the spirit of his mouth and “the brightness of his coming” that destroys the Wicked in 2 Thessalonians 2.

Paul says the Wicked's “coming is after the working of Satan.” Our comings are supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings are after Satan, and that goes back to Genesis 4.

The Lord speaks to Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Then the speech switches. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: now he is talking to Satan. Cain's desire shall be unto Satan, “and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over Cain.

So from the beginning Cain was put under Satan's rule, and his line has walked after Satan ever since. That is why the coming of the man of sin is “after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: he is following the one who was set to rule over his father.

“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” This is the same power Paul describes when the Lord consumes that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” God's word is the fire and the hammer.

In the same way, we don't see the word working in the spirit, but it is working. When it is spoken it breaks the rock in pieces, whether the hearer receives it or not.

That is why we must use God's word and not our own eloquence. Those who reject it are condemned by it, and when Christ comes, that same word destroys the Wicked by the brightness of his coming.

Paul says the Wicked shall be revealed, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of God's mouth is the holy Bible, and Jeremiah 5:14 shows how it consumes: “behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.”

Some of us speak very well and have eloquent words, and that is fine, but we must use God's word; that is where the power is. We read the Bible but don't see the spiritual effect it has in this realm, because our eyes are closed. God is saying, my word is fire. Speak it whether they hear or forbear. Even those who reject it are at home tossing and tumbling in their beds, because the way it is broken down haunts them.

As we teach the word of God, we are judging, and many are being marked for death. Everyone who hears it and rejects it and refuses it: remember that Christ said it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah than for those who do not hear his messengers. The words are the fire, the people who reject them are the wood, and that is how the Lord consumes the wicked with the spirit of his mouth.

Christ said this to the Pharisees, who were so in love with Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The lusts are the desires; they will do whatever their father desires.

“He was a murderer from the beginning”: that is Cain, not the spiritual demon. Cain murdered Abel. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.” Cain is a liar and the father of lies. Why? Because Satan is his father; Satan is his daddy.

This ties to Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and to 2 Thessalonians 2:9, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.” The line of Cain comes and goes after Satan, murdering and lying, just as their father did.

The Wicked comes “with all power and signs and lying wonders”, and Christ warned of the same: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.”

The great signs and wonders go with their science and their technology. Something major is going to happen. No one knows when, but before this kingdom goes down there is going to be a worldwide event to deceive the world, and some of us, God forbid, will be deceived by it.

That is why we must hold to God's word. The lying wonders come after the working of Satan, and only the word, the fire in our mouths, will keep us from being taken in when they come.

“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That is Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and it is 2 Thessalonians 2, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.”

The wicked man has Satan standing at his right hand, and he follows everything Satan says. That is why his coming is with “all power and signs and lying wonders”: it is Satan's working carried out through the man he rules.

So the scriptures line up from the beginning to the end: Cain under Satan's rule, the Pharisees doing the lusts of their father the devil, and the man of sin coming after the working of Satan, until the Lord consumes him with the spirit of his mouth.

Revelation 13 describes the same working Paul does: “he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men.” That fire coming down from heaven is thermonuclear fire.

“And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do.” See what it calls them: miracles. Those are the signs and wonders. It says the same thing Matthew 24 says and 2 Thessalonians 2 says, “signs and lying wonders”, only with a different word.

So the Wicked's coming after the working of Satan shows up as their science and their weapons, fire from heaven that looks like miracles, used to deceive the world. The Lord will consume him with the spirit of his mouth and destroy him with the brightness of his coming.

When the twins were born, Jacob came out and “his hand took hold on Esau’s heel.” That is very important, because there is a lot of symbolism behind it, and 2 Esdras 6 explains it.

Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first, and the beginning of it that followeth?” In other words, when shall this world end, and when shall the new world come in? The answer goes straight to Rebekah's womb: “From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.”

That is what the hand on the heel means. Esau's world is the one that ends, and Jacob's is the one that follows. It matches what the Lord told Rebekah: “Two nations are in thy womb”, “the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.” The word Genesis means beginning, and this is the beginning of those two nations.

Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important. It is not about Ruth, the Moabite heathen woman; y'all make it about her because y'all love heathens.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.
The trees “shall overshadow Israel” because “God shall lead Israel with joy”. Overshadow means to lead, so the Highest overshadowing Mary was the Lord leading her way.
A woman who “have conceived seed” conceives through her husband. So “thou shalt conceive in thy womb” uses the same plain language of seed and birth.
Mary asked “How shall this be”, for “how can a man then understand his own way”? The Lord guided her steps, as he guides every one of us.
The words “conceive in thy womb” speak of conception as it always happens: when Boaz went in unto Ruth, “the Lord gave her conception”. To conceive takes seed, and the Lord gives it.

To overshadow is to lead, guide and defend, like “a cloud shadowing the camp” as Israel crossed the sea. So “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee” means the Lord would guide Mary to her husband.

Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

God commands the brothers: “set thy face against the daughters of thy people, which prophesy out of their own heart; and prophesy thou against them.” Sisters say, you're always getting on the sisters. We get on you because the white man has tricked you and you have been deceived, and because you play an important role in rebuilding the nation. For the last sixty years the white man has used you to destroy the black community. So God says, set your face against these liberal women, the free thinkers who want to do whatever they want.

They prophesy out of their own heart, their own emotions: I don't feel it's wrong to wear pants; I don't see anything wrong with a blonde wig; Jesus loves everybody. No. Do what God says: wear skirts, and don't wear what pertains to a man. We prophesy against you so that you will see your wrongs and change, and so that the damage the white man has done to our community through our sisters can be undone.

Look at the decayed state of the liberal woman. One says there's nothing wrong with being an angry black woman; if she is angry she will raise her voice, twist her face and snap her neck. No sister should come with that spirit. That is no way to speak to your husband, or to anyone. Another had a man paying all the bills and taking care of her and the children, and she left him because she needed clarity and to find herself. Another left her husband of more than ten years because they outgrew each other, because he wanted her home and she wanted her career. Some sisters did the same and have repented: they left their husband thinking there was something better out there, and the next man did the same thing the first one did.

Genesis 2:18 shows what God made the woman to be: “It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” When God created woman, he said she is a help meet unto Adam, a good help. That is scriptural. Brothers, you want a woman who will help you build the kingdom, who will help build your dreams and help establish the kingdom of heaven. The liberal woman wants the benefit of a king without the patience or the work of helping him build.

That is what the civil rights did to our people. When this happens across the whole community, sons grow up with no father in the house and baby mamas instead of wives, and these things help destroy a community. Many sisters don't want accountability or responsibility, and there is a lot of work to do.

Purifying is more than staying from the sanctuary. Esther's “days of their purifications” took oils, sweet odours and help, and a new mother's “days of her purifying” are rest, care and good food to restore her body.
blog/2026/2026-09-27-2026-09-27-the-imag:
The attributes of the image were placed in us before the world had its say, and Exodus 11:7 shows how God guards his people: “But against any of the children of Israel shall not a dog move his tongue, against man or beast: that ye may know how that the Lord doth put a difference between the Egyptians and Israel.”

Are we the children of Israel? Then not a dog shall open its lips against us. No one can talk against us or anything that belongs to us. The Lord put a difference so that the world may know. We are his holy jewels, the jewellery God will wear around his neck, the apple of his eye. When they speak against us, they are speaking against his jewels and his people.

Carry yourselves like that, and never mind people who say you can't boast. Even in captivity: it is only temporary. We are not the finished product of what they did to us. A day is coming when this will be gone, and everything that ever spoke against our people will face judgment. They say, you don't talk like a slave. That is because we are not slaves.

Be like Christ. On the cross, he knew he could call down legions to wipe them out in the blink of an eye, because he already had the power, and he says we will be joint heirs with him. The world is scared to death that we will ever make that connection. They do not want us connected to that kind of power.

You were created with intention: not randomly formed, not accidentally designed, not undefined in purpose. You have a purpose; you just lost your way. “So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them. And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” Replenish the earth means have babies.

This is the original declaration, not only about humanity in general but about you specifically, the real soul of man and woman. Not the whore, the drug addict, the drug dealer they told you that you are. The real you is about righteousness, and you cannot define yourself by the conditioning of how you have been made to look. Conditioning says, we want to make a slave out of him, out of her, and make them think that is what they innately are. That is the point of saying the Negro was created in a lab: the real him has not stood up yet, the real us has not even surfaced yet.

You were made in the image of God, not in the image of your dysfunction. Not the image of your traumatic experiences, even though we have been through all kinds of trauma. Not the image crafted by an unstable childhood, an abusive relationship, or an environment that never reflected your worth back to you. Where it was said that we are not his people, it shall be said that we are the sons and daughters of God. We are not what they say we are; we are what God said we are. Carry yourselves that way and teach it to your children, because this world will turn them upside down if you are not serious about it.

Before conditioning entered, before survival strategies developed, before the false self was built, there was an image, an original design, and that design carries attributes: the capacity for creativity, for dominion, the capacity to rule, and for fruitfulness, children and nationhood. These are not just aspirations, like a novel we read. They are original; they are in our DNA, placed in us before the world opened its lips to say anything. When people see what we build and say it must be a sellout, that is a dysfunctional mind that believes we can't do anything. Men and women, whatever you went through, you can fix it. In IUIC we told everyone who said we couldn't to go to hell, and we did what we had to do.

“This people have I formed for myself; they shall shew forth my praise.” This people is the Israelites, Judah: God formed us for himself, to show forth his praise, and all the other nations will catch hell.

Put that in your spirit and put it in your children's spirit. Teach your children they are superior, because they are. The world tells us lies: it shows us Superman and Batman and all kinds of fools on TV and makes us think we are nothing but criminals. Then, when we say the reverse, they try the Jedi mind trick and make us think we are doing something wrong. That is why sons need fathers in the household who think this way, so they grow up in the right posture.

We were not formed for survival or to be a product of our environment. We were formed for a purpose that comes from outside our circumstances, connected to the nature and intent of the Most High who formed us. That is Jeremiah 1:5: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Before the sperm hit the egg, we already existed and were known by him, and he chose which spirit to send, this one rather than that one, for a purpose. “and I ordained thee a prophet unto the nations”: whatever the Lord ordained us to be, we will be. He made us the children of Israel and put talents in us. That is why those talents must be organized and not wasted. Don't bring self-doubt; get the doubt out and let the real you stay and be built up.

The foundational question is: am I who I was created to be, or am I what I was conditioned to become? It is not a surface-level question; it is an identity question that deals with the real soul of man and woman. Everything about us, our patterns, our responses, our beliefs, our defenses, has been shaped by one of two forces: creation or conditioning. Creation speaks to design; conditioning speaks to experience. One is intentional, the other reactive. One reflects origin, the image God made; the other reflects adaptation, to slavery, to ghettos, to being taken advantage of, to being unclean, a gang member, a drug addict. That is not who we really are, and most people live somewhere in between without ever telling the two apart.

Paul shows that fight in Romans 7:15: “For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.” What he ends up doing, the real him does not allow. What his spirit would do, the conditioned self will not follow. And what the real him hates, the righteous part connected to God that hates evil, he does anyway, acting from conditioning and not from what the Lord made him to be. “If then I do that which I would not, I consent unto the law that it is good.” That duality goes on with us every day.

Christ said you must deny yourself. The you that does the denying is the part God is dealing with; the self is the composite of the conditioning you were made into. So examine your own thoughts and behaviors and ask: why am I behaving like this? Is this the real me, or a response to what I have been conditioned to be?

Most of the time when we deal with our people, we are dealing with the mask, the representative, like the man holding up a sign in front of himself. The real soul is buried and scared, hiding under a tarp of trauma, lies, deceit and psychological hang-ups. The greatness buried under self-doubt has not surfaced yet. That is what is meant by the Negro being made in a lab: the real him has not stood up. We have to encourage that real spirit to come forward and be the image God made.
